scopeClasses.description: Slack reviews nothing before other workspaces can install an unlisted app. The catch is a throttle: apps created after 29 May 2025 that are not Marketplace approved read channel history at 1 request a minute.

claims.text: slack.com publishes an OpenID discovery document for Sign in with Slack, with the authorize endpoint https://slack.com/openid/connect/authorize and three scopes (openid, profile, email). The bot and user token flow uses a different endpoint, so the discovery document does not describe it.
claims.label: tested

probes.summary: Discovery document found for Sign in with Slack: authorize https://slack.com/openid/connect/authorize, token https://slack.com/api/openid.connect.token, 3 scopes, no PKCE methods listed.
Probe could not run: slack.com disallows automated fetching of the authorize endpoint (robots).

steps.title: Sign in to Slack and create the app at api.slack.com/apps
inputs: A Slack account and a development workspace

steps.title: Add the bot and user scopes you need and set an HTTPS redirect URL
steps.detail: Scopes are named in the OAuth flow and shown on the install screen. Keep the list short; workspace owners read it when approving apps.
inputs: Redirect URL from your auth config

steps.title: Implement the OAuth 2.0 flow and serve every app URL over SSL
steps.detail: Exchange the code at oauth.v2.access with the client secret. Composio's connect flow does this for you when you use the auth config.
inputs: Client ID and client secret in your auth config

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: From that moment any workspace can install from an Add to Slack button or a shareable install URL. No review.

steps.title: Design around the history throttle
steps.detail: If the app was created after 29 May 2025 and is not Marketplace approved, conversations.history and conversations.replies run at 1 request a minute with 15 objects per call. Use events and webhooks for new messages rather than polling history.
inputs: Your read pattern for channel history

steps.title: Prepare customers for workspace approval
steps.detail: Workspaces with app approval on will route your install to an owner. Give users a one paragraph description and the scope list for that request.
inputs: A short approval note for workspace owners

steps.title: Only if you want the Marketplace listing or the full rate limits: reach 10 active workspaces, then submit
steps.detail: Submission needs a privacy policy, a support channel answering within 2 business days, a 30 to 90 second demo video and, for LLM features, the model disclosure. Resubmitting during preliminary review resets your queue place.

steps.title: Submit the Marketplace listing and plan for the review wait
steps.detail: Slack states up to 10 business days for preliminary feedback and up to 10 weeks for functional review. One developer reports four months end to end in 2026.

playbooks.symptom: Your agent reads channel history and gets rate limited almost immediately.
playbooks.cause: The app was created after 29 May 2025 and is not approved for the Marketplace, so conversations.history and conversations.replies run at 1 request a minute, 15 objects a call.
playbooks.fix: Switch to the Events API for new messages and cache history. If you need bulk history, the Marketplace review is the path to the normal limits, and it needs 10 active workspaces first.

playbooks.symptom: A customer clicks Add to Slack and lands on a request for approval instead of the consent screen.
playbooks.cause: Their workspace has app approval enabled.
playbooks.fix: Have the customer send the approval request to a workspace owner, and give them a one paragraph description plus the scope list.

playbooks.symptom: Your Marketplace submission keeps going back to the end of the queue.
playbooks.cause: Every resubmission during preliminary review resets your place.
playbooks.fix: Fix every item in the feedback before resubmitting, and do not touch the submission while it is in preliminary review.
